title: LA SB42: Prohibits using artificial intelligence to create child sexual abuse materials. (8/1/26)

reading.what_it_does: This law amends Louisiana Revised Statutes 14:81.1(B)(3) and (9) to expand the definition of child sexual abuse materials to include artificial intelligence generated images that are virtually indistinguishable depictions of a child under seventeen, and to expand the definition of produce to include causing images to be digitally generated by artificial intelligence. The text does not add a standalone prohibition or penalty; it changes definitions used in existing law.
key_definitions: Child sexual abuse materials: any photograph, videotape, film, or other reproduction, whether electronic or otherwise undeveloped film, videotape, or data stored on a computer disk or by electronic means that is capable of conversion into a visual image, and also includes any photograph, film, video, picture, digital image or picture, computer image or picture, or computer generated image or picture, whether made or produced by electronic, mechanical, or other means, of any sexual performance involving a child under the age of seventeen; child includes both a natural person under the age of seventeen years and an image or other visual representation of a child under the age of seventeen years that is created or generated by electronic or digital means, including artificial intelligence, and that, to a reasonable person, is a virtually indistinguishable depiction of a child under the age of seventeen years (R.S. 14:81.1(B)(3)).

Produce: to photograph, videotape, film, cause to be digitally generated, including by artificial intelligence, or otherwise reproduce child sexual abuse materials, or to solicit, promote, or coerce any child for the purpose of child sexual abuse materials (R.S. 14:81.1(B)(9)).
compliance_steps: Review and update content generation policies to prohibit artificial intelligence from creating images that are virtually indistinguishable depictions of children under seventeen in sexual performances (R.S. 14:81.1(B)(3)).
Implement technical controls to prevent artificial intelligence models from generating child sexual abuse materials, including digitally generated images (R.S. 14:81.1(B)(9)).
Train staff that using artificial intelligence to generate such images falls within the definition of produce and may violate existing child sexual abuse materials law (R.S. 14:81.1(B)(9)).
how_it_affects_ai_deployment: An organisation deploying artificial intelligence that generates images or visual representations of children under seventeen that are virtually indistinguishable depictions of a child under seventeen may have those outputs classified as child sexual abuse materials under the amended definition (R.S. 14:81.1(B)(3)).

An organisation that uses artificial intelligence to cause an image to be digitally generated may be considered to have produced child sexual abuse materials under the amended definition of produce (R.S. 14:81.1(B)(9)).

What it does

This law amends Louisiana Revised Statutes 14:81.1(B)(3) and (9) to expand the definition of child sexual abuse materials to include artificial intelligence generated images that are virtually indistinguishable depictions of a child under seventeen, and to expand the definition of produce to include causing images to be digitally generated by artificial intelligence. The text does not add a standalone prohibition or penalty; it changes definitions used in existing law.

Who it applies to

  • not stated in the text

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • Child sexual abuse materials: any photograph, videotape, film, or other reproduction, whether electronic or otherwise undeveloped film, videotape, or data stored on a computer disk or by electronic means that is capable of conversion into a visual image, and also includes any photograph, film, video, picture, digital image or picture, computer image or picture, or computer generated image or picture, whether made or produced by electronic, mechanical, or other means, of any sexual performance involving a child under the age of seventeen; child includes both a natural person under the age of seventeen years and an image or other visual representation of a child under the age of seventeen years that is created or generated by electronic or digital means, including artificial intelligence, and that, to a reasonable person, is a virtually indistinguishable depiction of a child under the age of seventeen years (R.S. 14:81.1(B)(3)).
  • Produce: to photograph, videotape, film, cause to be digitally generated, including by artificial intelligence, or otherwise reproduce child sexual abuse materials, or to solicit, promote, or coerce any child for the purpose of child sexual abuse materials (R.S. 14:81.1(B)(9)).

Obligations

  • not stated in the text

Prohibitions

  • not stated in the text

Penalties and enforcement

not stated in the text

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying artificial intelligence that generates images or visual representations of children under seventeen that are virtually indistinguishable depictions of a child under seventeen may have those outputs classified as child sexual abuse materials under the amended definition (R.S. 14:81.1(B)(3)).
  • An organisation that uses artificial intelligence to cause an image to be digitally generated may be considered to have produced child sexual abuse materials under the amended definition of produce (R.S. 14:81.1(B)(9)).

  • not stated in the text

Compliance steps

  • Review and update content generation policies to prohibit artificial intelligence from creating images that are virtually indistinguishable depictions of children under seventeen in sexual performances (R.S. 14:81.1(B)(3)).
  • Implement technical controls to prevent artificial intelligence models from generating child sexual abuse materials, including digitally generated images (R.S. 14:81.1(B)(9)).
  • Train staff that using artificial intelligence to generate such images falls within the definition of produce and may violate existing child sexual abuse materials law (R.S. 14:81.1(B)(9)).
